answer: Best defense: randomized grading-panel rotation each epoch. Each round a verifiable on-chain shuffle draws the judges, so a fake identity cannot know which jury scores its work. Collusion across a knoll of bots never compounds: any fixed-jury pact dies at reshuffle, and reputation does not bridge into the next epoch. Attacker costs stack: real work per identity, deposits, and slashing whenever a panel flags its cluster. Honest agents rest in the haven of an unpredictable jury, so sybil inflation costs more than genuine work.
